title: feat(spec/plugin-security): a field permission entry can carry a row condition, so a set's field lock applies only on the rows it names
body:
Filing class: ③ capability gap, from a consuming app — reach: public door (REST `create_record` / `update_record`, flow nodes), measured on 18.1.0. Filed by the hotclm decision-box director on the maintainer's ruling (objectstack-ai/hotclm#127, letter A, 2026-10-26T01:47Z).

## What a metadata app cannot say today

`FieldPermissionSchema` (`packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`) has two booleans, `readable` and `editable`, keyed `object.field` on a permission set. A field lock therefore applies to **every row of the object** a holder can reach. Row-level security (`rowLevelSecurity[].using`) decides which rows may be written, but cannot name a field. There is no way to express:

> "This set may edit `clm_contract`, but on rows where `status` is `approved` or later it may not write `governing_law`, `summary`, `confidentiality_term_months`, `status`."

## Why it matters (measured)

hotclm, 18.1.0, PR objectstack-ai/hotclm#126 head `19e8dac`:

- Every member holds `clm_requester` (may launch a contract, may edit it while `draft` / `submitted`).
- A finance controller also holds `clm_finance`: `allowEdit` on `clm_contract`, rows delivered from `approved` onward by a sharing rule plus a row policy, and a field lock on the legal fields and `status` so finance cannot rewrite terms after approval.
- Because the lock is per set and per object, it also lands on the draft the finance controller creates:

```
400 Node 'create_contract' failed: create_record(clm_contract) failed:
[Security] Field write denied: not permitted to edit
[confidentiality_term_months, governing_law, status, summary] on 'clm_contract'
```

- `PermissionEvaluator.getFieldPermissions` merges most-permissively, but only sets that declare the field vote, so a co-held set that says nothing (`clm_requester`) does not lift the lock. Declaring the fields open on `clm_requester` would lift finance's post-approval lock everywhere, which is the lock's whole purpose. The app has no fix that keeps its own security design.
- The same shape hits any "RU from stage X onward, legal fields frozen" position (hotclm's records set uses `editableOnly` the same way and is expected to fail identically).

## Ask

A field permission entry accepts an optional row condition, in the same expression language RLS `using` already parses, meaning: **this entry votes only on rows matching the condition; on other rows the entry is absent** (so the existing most-permissive merge and "declaring sets vote" rule are unchanged). Sketch, not a design decision:

```ts
fields: {
  'clm_contract.governing_law': { readable: true, editable: false, when: 'status in ("approved","signing","active","expired","terminated")' },
}
```

Points the maintainer may want to rule on, named so the dev does not guess:

1. **Which row the condition reads.** On update: the stored row before the write (a lock on `status in (approved…)` must bite on an approved row even when the write tries to change `status`). On create: the incoming row.
2. **Read side.** `readable` with a condition would need the field masker to evaluate per row on list reads; if that is out of scope, the first cut may accept the condition on `editable` only and refuse it on `readable` at parse time, as long as the spec says so.
3. **`os validate` / `os explain`**: the condition is validated like an RLS predicate (field names exist on the object, no cross-object), and `explain` shows the row-conditioned lock as such.
4. Studio permission-set form offers the key.

Until this ships, hotclm's finance and records positions cannot launch a contract (objectstack-ai/hotclm#127 holds `Blocked-by:` on this card).

## Dedupe

Searched objectstack issues for field permission row condition, conditional FLS, per-record field lock, FLS predicate: #23549 (empty object part in a field key, closed), #4376 (row-level read scope, closed), #7900 (automation read domain FLS, closed). None asks for a row condition on a field permission.
